t: #2508 Add Edges to Make Degrees of All Nodes Even
o: Adding an edge toggles the parity of its two endpoints, so we must fix the odd-degree vertices using at most 2 edges (each fixes exactly 2). Let k = number of odd vertices. k must be 0, 2, or 4. k=0: done. k=2 (a,b): either add edge (a,b) if absent, or find an even-degree node c with both (a,c),(c,b) absent. k=4 (a,b,c,d): try the three perfect matchings, checking both edges are absent. Example 3 has 3 odd vertices → impossible. Existence checks use a hash set of normalized edge keys.
k: Each added edge flips parity of exactly two nodes, so #odd ∈ {0,2,4} is necessary.
For 2 odd nodes, a helper node must have even degree (stays even after +2) and both new edges must not already exist.
Try all three pairings for 4 odd nodes.

a.n: Approach 1: Case analysis on odd-degree vertices
a.i: Count odd vertices; handle the 0/2/4 cases with direct or helper-edge attempts, validating against an edge-existence set.
s: Build degree array and edge set keyed by (min,max).
If 0 odd → true; if >4 odd → false.
2 odd (a,b): true if (a,b) absent; else scan for even-degree c ∉ {a,b} with (a,c),(c,b) absent.
4 odd: check matchings (ab,cd),(ac,bd),(ad,bc) for absence; return accordingly.
a.t: O(n + m) — degree counting plus one linear scan for the helper node in the 2-odd case.
a.sp: O(n + m) for degrees and the edge set.

w: One approach covers it — the value is entirely in the case analysis. Pitfalls: forgetting the helper node must currently have EVEN degree, allowing self-loops or duplicate edges (always normalize and check the set), and missing that 4 odd vertices cannot share a helper (each edge fixes exactly 2). Follow-up: allow k edges (matching theory), or directed graphs (in/out degree balance).
